extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors and page designers (and general New York Times readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and principles for newspaper page makeup/layout and the editorial motto guiding what to publish on a New York Times page (balance, placement of cuts, use of heads/boxes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Make-Up 225
rubrics_metrics.description: PRINCIPLES OF MAKE-UP 225 (page heading referencing rules for page composition and makeup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains explicit discussion of page composition and balance (see entries below). On this page the placing of the cut at the top center; the arrangement of heads and boxes; and different forms of balance are used to achieve an effective page makeup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetrical balance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aids the symmetry. (Text: "Symmetrical balance. ... aids the symmetry.") — used as a named principle for arranging page elements so both sides mirror or balance each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of the cut at the top center
rubrics_metrics.description: On this page the placing of the cut at the top center
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing a cut (image) at the top center is cited as a compositional choice that affects the overall balance of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Slightly occult balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Slightly occult balance. Note how this plate differs from plates I and II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained by example: "The two-column head and the small box at the right are balanced by the longer box." (i.e., use unequal elements positioned to achieve visual equilibrium — two-column head + small right box balanced by a longer box elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements of Journalism (editorial principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: "All the News That's Fit to Print." (The New York Times motto / editorial standard.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as the paper's guiding editorial principle for selection and presentation of news; functions as a high-level criterion for what material belongs on the page.
